itens.titulo: Is Intel Stock a Buy After Its Post-Earnings Plunge?
itens.descricao: Is Intel Stock a Buy After Its Post-Earnings Plunge? Yahoo Finance
trechos: Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) stock dropped about 23% in after-hours trading on Thursday, Oct.
29, after the company released its third-quarter numbers.
Shares that closed the regular session at $92.07 traded around $71 by the end of the evening.
Revenue grew 21% year over year to $16.5 billion.
And non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share of $0.52 came in far above the $0.38 management had guided for in July, more than doubling from $0.23 a year before.
In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia.
For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia.
Intel forecast fourth-quarter revenue at $15.0 billion to $16.0 billion and adjusted earnings per share at $0.25 -- under half what it just earned.

itens.titulo: Why Bitcoin’s Next All-Time High Looks Distant After the Binance Hack
itens.descricao: Why Bitcoin’s Next All-Time High Looks Distant After the Binance Hack Yahoo Finance
trechos: The biggest theft in crypto history, the $6.3 billion Binance hack, is already showing its scar on the crypto market.
After a month of moving between the $80,000 and $85,000 range, Bitcoin has dropped to $76,000 since the incident.
"If the king can't protect itself, how can any other exchange be trusted?
The answer to all of the above is they can't." Edwards argues that AI-driven exploits now outpace security patches.
He pointed to Tether halting $1.8 billion of the stolen funds as proof that crypto needs human intervention.
"I said early this year, Bitcoin won't get a new ATH until a Core governed Quantum Proof roadmap is established.
ATH's are looking more and more distant today." Roughly 80 minutes later, he went further.

itens.descricao: Why Micron Stock Dove Today Yahoo Finance
trechos: Shares of Micron (NASDAQ:MU) stumbled out of the gate Friday morning, falling as much as 5.9%.
ET, the stock was still down 4.7%.
In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia.
For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia.
For its fiscal 2027 first quarter (ended Oct.
2), the company delivered revenue that soared 378% year over year and 23% quarter over quarter to $11 billion.
This fueled adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $49.51, which grew more than 40-fold.
For context, analysts' consensus estimates were for revenue of $10.7 billion and adjusted EPS of $46.67, so the company cleared both hurdles by a wide margin.
